evidence.quote: Within that framework, I would have been comfortable with the FOMC's beginning to taper its asset purchases at the September meeting.
It was a close call for me, but I did so because I continue to support our efforts to create a highly accommodative monetary environment

And if we push the recruits very hard--as we arguably have over the past year or so--it is probably more likely that we are going to see a change in their behavior and hence a sharp movement in rates at some point.
On net, I believe the adjustment has been a healthy one.
For example, one could cut monthly purchases by a set amount for each further 10 basis point decline in the unemployment rate.

parsed.rationale: Stein says he would have been comfortable beginning to taper in September and calls the hold a close call. He also stresses the financial-stability costs of pushing term premiums down and welcomes the rise in yields, a moderately hawkish lean despite his continued support for accommodation.
